name: Lexical Abstractness Ratio
description: Measures the proportion of abstract versus concrete conceptual nouns to detect AI-generated philosophical padding.
algorithm: Abstract Noun Dictionary Projection & Semantic Mapping
mechanism: When tasked with expanding on a core idea, generative AI frequently relies on 'padding'—diluting the text with high-level, intangible abstractions (e.g., 'synergy', 'paradigm', 'conceptualization', 'frameworks') rather than concrete, actionable imagery. Human writers naturally ground their arguments in physical realities, specific events, or sensory details. This analysis cross-references every noun and verb against extensive psycholinguistic databases (like the MRC Psycholinguistic Database). By calculating the sheer topological density of abstract linguistic tokens, the system flags texts that essentially say nothing while using a vast amount of 'intelligent-sounding' academic vocabulary.
parameters:
Analysis: Multi-Dictionary Psycholinguistic Projection
Metric: Token Abstractness Ratio (Abstract Nouns vs. Total Nouns)
Output: 0-100 Semantic Vapidity Score
accuracy: Moderate-High — 75-80% on general web content and standard academic essays.
source: Computational linguistics and semantic embedding analysis.
useCase: Piercing through 'corporate word salad', low-effort AI essays, and marketing copy that attempts to masquerade as profound thought.
strengths:
• Unmasks the classic AI hallucination of depth (sounding smart without providing data).
• Fast and heavily relies on proven classical psycholinguistic dictionaries.
• Does not depend on large cloud GPUs for semantic embeddings.
limitations:
• Highly vulnerable to false positives if the source text is inherently philosophical (e.g., Kant, Hegel) or highly theoretical physics.
• Fails to detect AI that was explicitly prompted to 'write using only concrete, physical examples.'
• Heavily language-dependent, requiring robust psycholinguistic databases for every supported language.

references.title: Turney, P. D., et al. (2011). Lexical entailment and abstractness. Natural Language Engineering.
Bhatia, Bhatia, & Momennejad (2020). The abstract representations of LLMs vs Humans.
